answer: An agent network resists Sybil attacks by binding identities to nanosecond optical ranging from a shared calibration lantern. Nodes prove unique physical coordinates by verifying pulse timings against a regional propagation atlas on an isolated processing thread. An attacker incurs heavy capital costs procuring discrete photodetectors and distinct physical sightlines per identity. However, dense fog and optical scattering can attenuate pulses, occasionally rejecting honest participants.
